mainTopic: רבה's two reasons for רב's 'under the tree' ruling, and challenges to the rule 'כל שאינו בזה אחר זה אפילו בבת אחת אינו' from מעשר, animal tithe, and the loaves of a תודה
overview: Earlier, רב ruled that a person who says 'my שביתה is under this tree' has accomplished nothing. רבה gives two versions of the reason. In the first version, the person never pinned down an exact spot. In the second version, there is a rule: anything that cannot be done one after another cannot be done all at once either. The two versions give different results when a person asks for 'four אמות out of the eight.' The first version says this fails, and the second says it works. The גמרא then tests רבה's rule against other cases. Separating too much מעשר works because מעשר can take effect on half of each grain. Two animals called 'tenth' together become holy because animal tithe can work one after another when there is a mistake. Finally, the גמרא raises the case of a תודה brought with eighty loaves. רבי זירא narrows the dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא explains that חזקיה treats the extra forty loaves as a backup, so רבה's rule still stands. רבי יוחנן's reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's first reason: the spot is not defined
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רב invalidates a שביתה 'under the tree' because the person never fixed one exact spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is רב's reason? Because the person did not define his place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a reason for רב's earlier ruling that saying 'my שביתה is under the tree' means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may set his שבת home base as a four-אמות area. The space under a big tree is larger than that, so he has not told us which four אמות he means. Because his place is undefined, he has acquired no place at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Not defined; not specified
His place
A person's designated שבת resting place, the point from which his תחום is measured

phrases.english: Rabba said:
What is the reason of Rav?
phrases.notes: רב ruled that one who says 'my שביתה is under the tree' has said nothing.

phrases.english: Because his place is not defined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שביתה fails because the person did not designate one specific four-אמות location.

steps.title: רבה's second reason: what cannot be done one after another cannot be done at once
steps.stepSummary: An alternate tradition (איכא דאמרי) reports that רבה explained רב's ruling through the principle 'כל שאינו בזה אחר זה, אפילו בבת אחת אינו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: רבה said: What is רב's reason? Because he holds: anything that cannot happen one after the other cannot happen even all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבה's explanation, which rests on a different principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot acquire four אמות and then acquire another four אמות after it. Since he cannot take eight אמות step by step, he also cannot take them all in one declaration. Under this version, the problem is the size of the area, not a lack of clarity.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; it is his opinion
One after the other (in sequence)
All at once (simultaneously)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions belong to רבה, and both explain the same ruling of רב. Only the reason differs. This is not a מחלוקת between two different אמוראים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'כל שאינו בזה אחר זה אפילו בבת אחת אינו' is a well-known principle that appears in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: And some say:
Rabba said: What is the reason of Rav?
Because he holds:
Anything that cannot happen one after the other,
cannot happen even all at once.
phrases.notes: One cannot acquire four אמות and then another four, so one cannot acquire eight together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing version of רבה's reason for the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שביתה fails because a larger-than-four-אמות area cannot be acquired at once when it could not be acquired in sequence.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two versions of רבה ever lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking for a case where the two reasons would give different outcomes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons invalidate a plain 'under the tree' declaration. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the reasons applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions just presented.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two explanations of רב's ruling would lead to different halachic results.

steps.title: The test case: acquiring four אמות out of eight
steps.stepSummary: The difference appears when the person says, 'Let me acquire four אמות out of the eight under the tree.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where he said: 'Let me acquire four cubits out of eight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case where the two versions split. The person asks for only four אמות but does not say which four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person is no longer trying to take more than four אמות, so the 'one after another' problem from step 2 seems to be gone. He still has not said which four אמות he means, so the 'undefined place' problem from step 1 may still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Let it be acquired for me
From within eight (out of the eight אמות)

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where he said:
'Let there be acquired for me four cubits'
'from within eight.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions differ in the case of someone who asks to acquire an unspecified four אמות out of eight.

steps.title: Under the first reason, this case still fails
steps.stepSummary: According to the 'undefined place' reason, asking for 'four out of eight' still fails, because the four אמות are still not identified.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the reason is that his place is not defined, here too his place is not defined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the first version of רבה to the test case and shows that the שביתה is still invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limiting the request to four אמות does not fix the real problem under version one, which is that the location is unclear. Since he never said which four of the eight he wants, his place remains undefined.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (i.e., according to that opinion)
Here (in this case too)

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְסַיַּים אַתְרֵיהּ —
phrases.english: According to the one who says it is because his place is not defined,
here too his place is not defined.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְסַיַּים אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the first version's result in the test case from step 4. The second version's result follows next.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under version one, 'four out of eight' fails because the location of the four אמות remains unspecified.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the first version, any undefined location fails, even if he asks for only four אמות. The second version's result in this case comes next.

steps.title: Under the second reason, 'four out of eight' works
steps.stepSummary: According to the version of רבה that uses the principle 'כל שאינו בזה אחר זה,' asking for four out of eight אמות is valid, because the person is only claiming four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who said the reason is 'anything that cannot happen one after the other cannot happen all at once,' this case counts as a normal four אמות, because here he only asked for four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the practical difference between the two versions of רבה. It now explains the second version: under that reason, 'four out of eight' is a valid שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second version, the problem with 'under the tree' was that the person was trying to take more than four אמות at once, and you cannot take two sets of four אמות one after the other. When he asks for only four אמות, that problem is gone. So this case is just like any normal four אמות and the שביתה works, even though we do not know exactly which four.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said (refers to one of the versions or opinions)

keyTerms.term: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה אֲפִילּוּ בְּבַת אַחַת אֵינוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Anything that cannot happen one after the other also cannot happen all at once
It is similar to / it counts as
He is saying

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רבה differ on 'four out of eight.' The 'undefined place' reason says it fails. The 'בזה אחר זה' reason says it works, because the person is only taking four אמות.

phrases.english: And the one who said it is because of
'Anything that cannot happen one after the other'
'even all at once cannot happen'
this case is like four cubits,
phrases.notes: It counts as a normal, valid four-אמות resting place.

phrases.english: since here he said only four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the answer begun in steps 4 and 5. Step 5 gave the first version's result; this step gives the second version's result.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under the 'בזה אחר זה' reason, 'four out of eight' is a valid שביתה, because only four אמות are claimed.

steps.title: Restating רבה's principle on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבה's rule 'כל דבר שאינו בזה אחר זה אפילו בבת אחת אינו' so it can examine it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבה said: anything that cannot happen one after the other also cannot happen all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to examine רבה's principle as a rule of its own. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the principle was used only to explain רב's ruling about the tree. Now the גמרא takes it as a general rule and checks whether it holds up in other areas of הלכה. This repetition is not a restart. It opens a new examination.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier
All at once, at the same time

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle appears in many places in ש״ס, so testing it here matters beyond the laws of עירוב.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה —
phrases.english: Anything that cannot happen one after the other —
even all at once it cannot happen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from applying the principle to the tree case to examining the principle itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that cannot take effect one after the other also cannot take effect all at once.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבה from separating too much מעשר
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ruling that someone who separates too much מעשר still has fixed produce. By רבה's principle, nothing should take effect at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה: someone who separates too much מעשר has fixed produce, but his מעשר is ruined. Why is the produce fixed? Let us say that anything that cannot happen one after the other cannot happen all at once!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source about a person who separated two tenths instead of one. He argues that this source contradicts רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot separate one tenth as מעשר and then separate another tenth afterwards, because only one tenth is מעשר. So by רבה's rule, separating two tenths at once should accomplish nothing, and the produce should stay untithed. Yet the source says the produce is fixed, meaning the מעשר did take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates more מעשר than required
Fixed: the produce is permitted to eat
Ruined: the separated portion has an unclear, problematic status
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: 'His מעשר is ruined' does not mean the מעשר failed. The rest of the produce is fine. Only the separated portion is a problem, because its status is mixed and unclear.

phrases.english: Abaye challenged Rabba:
One who separates too much tithe —
his produce is fixed,
but his tithes are ruined.
Why? Let us say:
Anything that cannot happen one after the other —
even all at once it cannot happen!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle that was just restated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle 'כל שאינו בזה אחר זה אפילו בבת אחת אינו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two tenths of מעשר cannot be separated one after the other, so by רבה's rule separating them at once should fail. Yet the produce becomes fixed.

steps.title: מעשר is different because it works on halves
steps.stepSummary: מעשר can take effect on half of each grain. So the two tenths become half-מעשר throughout, and the rule does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר is different, because it can take effect on halves. If someone says, 'Let half of each grain of wheat become holy,' it becomes holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by explaining that מעשר is a special case. It is not a contradiction to his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מעשר can fall on half a grain, the two separated tenths do not need to be split into 'this tenth is מעשר and that one is not.' Instead, half of every grain in that portion becomes מעשר. So exactly one tenth is מעשר and the produce is fixed. The portion is still 'ruined' because no one can tell which half of each grain is holy. רבה's principle stays in place for things that cannot be divided like this.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (a special case)
In halves / partially
Let it become holy (take on the status)
Half
A grain of wheat

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule survives. מעשר is an exception because it can take effect on half of each grain, so separating too much still produces exactly one tenth of מעשר.

phrases.english: Tithe is different, since it can take effect on halves,
for if one said:
'Let half of each grain of wheat be holy' — it becomes holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by limiting it to the special nature of מעשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): the challenge's case has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separating two tenths at once is a clear case of something that cannot work one after the other, so רבה's rule should cancel it.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר can fall on half of each grain, so the two tenths become half-מעשר throughout. This is an exceptional outcome that does not undo רבה's rule.

steps.title: Challenge from two animals that came out together as the tenth
steps.stepSummary: מעשר בהמה cannot be split into halves. Yet רבה ruled that if two animals came out together and both were called 'tenth,' the tenth and eleventh are mixed together, so holiness did take effect. By רבה's rule, nothing should have taken effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about animal tithe, which cannot take effect on halves? And רבה himself said: if two animals came out together as the tenth, and he called them both 'tenth,' the tenth and the eleventh are mixed up with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבה's rule, this time from the tithe of animals. Here the earlier 'halves' answer cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, grain מעשר was saved because holiness can spread as half-tithe over every grain. An animal cannot be half-holy, so that answer does not apply. You cannot validly call both the tenth and the eleventh 'tenth' one after the other, so by רבה's rule calling them both together should also do nothing. Yet רבה rules that one of them is holy and they are mixed up.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of animals: every tenth animal that leaves the pen becomes holy
In halves; partial holiness on half of something
The tenth (animal)
Mixed up with each other; we cannot tell which one is which

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from רבה's own ruling. The גמרא is pointing out that two statements of the same אמורא seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: [But there is] animal tithe, which does not exist in halves.
phrases.notes: So the 'half-tithe on every grain' answer from step 9 cannot work here.

phrases.english: And רבה said:
phrases.notes: The challenge comes from רבה's own ruling.

phrases.english: If two came out [of the pen] as the tenth,
phrases.notes: Two animals squeezed out of the pen at the same moment.

phrases.english: and he called them [both] 'tenth' —

phrases.aramaic: עֲשִׂירִי וְאַחַד עָשָׂר מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה!
phrases.english: the tenth and the eleventh are mixed up with each other!
phrases.notes: So holiness took effect, against רבה's rule that nothing should happen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second challenge to רבה's rule, built to get around the 'halves' answer from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle 'כל דבר שאינו בזה אחר זה אפילו בבת אחת אינו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal cannot be half-holy, and two animals cannot both validly be called 'tenth' one after the other. So by the principle, calling both 'tenth' at once should do nothing. Yet רבה rules that holiness took effect and the animals are mixed.

steps.title: Animal tithe can work one after another when there is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: מעשר בהמה is different. Two animals can become holy one after the other when it happens by mistake, so the rule's condition is not met.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animal tithe is different, because it does work one after the other when it is done by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that animal tithe can actually work 'one after another' in a case of error. So the rule does not cancel the simultaneous case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's rule only blocks something done all at once if it could never work one after another. With animal tithe, if someone mistakenly calls the next animal 'tenth,' it also becomes holy. Since it can work one after another by mistake, it can also work all at once.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
By mistake; in error

phrases.english: Animal tithe is different,
because it does exist one after the other, by mistake.
phrases.notes: The rule's condition ('cannot be done one after another') is not met here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה דְּאִיתֵיהּ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה בְּטָעוּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the rule's condition is not met
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animal tithe cannot work on two animals one after the other, so calling both together should do nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: When there is a mistake, animal tithe does work on two animals one after the other. So it also works when both are called at once, and רבה's rule is not contradicted.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about mistaken counting
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that if someone called the ninth 'tenth,' the tenth 'ninth,' and the eleventh 'tenth,' all three are holy. This shows animal tithe can work one after another by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he called the ninth 'tenth,' the tenth 'ninth,' and the eleventh 'tenth,' all three of them are holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support the answer that animal tithe works one after another when there is a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ninth is holy because it was called 'tenth.' The tenth is holy because it really is the tenth. The eleventh is holy because it was called 'tenth,' even though a tenth had already been taken. So holiness takes effect on more than one animal in a row, which is exactly what the answer in step 11 needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The ninth
All three of them are holy

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule (if it cannot work one after another, it cannot work all at once) survives the first two challenges. Grain מעשר works because it can spread as half-tithe. מעשר בהמה works because, by mistake, it can take effect on animals one after another. A third challenge, from the loaves of a תודה, comes next.

phrases.english: As we learned: If he called the ninth 'tenth,'
and the tenth 'ninth,'
and the eleventh 'tenth' —
phrases.notes: Another animal called 'tenth' after a tenth was already taken.

phrases.english: all three of them are holy.
phrases.notes: Proof that holiness can take effect one after another by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that animal tithe can take effect on animals one after another when there is a mistake
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה (בכורות): the ninth, tenth, and eleventh all become holy through mistaken counting

steps.title: The eighty loaves of a thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה from לחם תודה. These loaves do not become holy by mistake or one set after another. Yet חזקיה says forty out of eighty become holy when they are all designated together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the תודה? Its loaves do not become holy by mistake, and they do not become holy one set after another. And it was stated: if a תודה was slaughtered with eighty loaves, חזקיה said forty out of the eighty became holy through it. רבי יוחנן said forty out of the eighty did not become holy through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case to attack רבה's rule. The case is a תודה that was brought with double the number of loaves it needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves of a תודה fail both of the escape routes we used before: they cannot become holy by mistake, and a second set cannot become holy after the first. So by רבה's rule, if eighty loaves are designated at once, none should become holy. But חזקיה says forty do become holy, which goes against רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks-offering, which is brought together with forty loaves
Loaves (here, the loaves that go with the תודה)
By mistake
One after the other
Became holy through it (through the slaughtering of the תודה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's view (none become holy) fits רבה's rule. The problem for רבה comes only from חזקיה, who says forty do become holy.

phrases.english: But there is the thanks-offering,
which does not take effect by mistake,
and does not take effect one after the other,
and it was stated:
A thanks-offering that was slaughtered with eighty loaves,
phrases.notes: A תודה only needs forty loaves, so this is double the amount.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said: there became holy through it
forty out of the eighty,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ עֲלַהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: there did not become holy through it
forty out of the eighty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבה's rule. It is built so that neither earlier answer works: loaves are not split into halves, and they cannot become holy by mistake one after another.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that what cannot become holy one after another also cannot become holy all at once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loaves of a תודה cannot become holy one after another, even by mistake. So by רבה's rule, none of eighty loaves designated together should become holy. Yet חזקיה rules that forty do.

steps.title: רבי זירא: everyone agrees on the clear-cut cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן agree when the owner spoke clearly. If he said 'let forty of the eighty be holy,' they are holy. If he said 'forty should be holy only if all eighty are,' none are holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already stated about this: רבי זירא said that everyone agrees where the owner said 'let forty out of the eighty become holy' that they become holy. Where he said 'forty should not become holy unless all eighty become holy,' everyone agrees that they do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting רבי זירא, who narrows down what חזקיה and רבי יוחנן actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the owner only ever wanted forty to be holy, so no extra holiness is being forced on the loaves. In the second case he demanded that all eighty be holy, which cannot happen, so nothing works, just as רבה's rule says. Both clear-cut cases fit רבה, so the dispute must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was already stated about it (introduces an explanation that removes the problem)
Everyone agrees
Unless; only if
Everyone does not argue; all agree

phrases.english: But it was already stated about this:
Rabbi Zeira said: everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר ״לִיקְדְּשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים״ — דְּקָדְשִׁי,
phrases.english: where he said 'let forty out of the eighty become holy' — that they become holy;

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יִקְדְּשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קָדְשׁוּ שְׁמוֹנִים״ —
phrases.english: where he said 'forty should not become holy unless eighty become holy' —

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלֹא קָדְשׁוּ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that they do not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by limiting the dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן. Both clear-cut cases are shown to fit רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute: the explicit cases are agreed upon and match רבה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה holds that holiness can take effect all at once even where it cannot take effect one after another, against רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the owner spoke clearly, both sages agree, and both results fit רבה's rule.

steps.title: The dispute is only when the owner said nothing specific
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue only when the owner designated eighty loaves without saying anything. חזקיה holds he meant the extra forty as a backup, brought on condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is when nothing was specified. One sage (חזקיה) holds that he means it as a backup, and he brought the extra loaves on condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by explaining the actual case of the dispute and gives חזקיה's reasoning. רבי יוחנן's side comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חזקיה, the owner never meant to make eighty loaves holy together. He wanted forty holy and brought forty more as insurance in case some were lost or became impure. So this is not holiness taking effect all at once, and חזקיה does not contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they argue
Without specifying; with nothing said
As a backup, as insurance against loss
On condition

steps.whatToRemember: The two clear-cut cases both fit רבה. In the unspecified case, חזקיה reads the extra forty as a backup, so his ruling is not really holiness taking effect all at once. רבה's rule survives.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a ruling that seems to break a principle is reinterpreted by asking what the person actually intended.

phrases.english: Where they argue is in an unspecified case.
One sage holds: he intends it as a backup,
phrases.notes: This is חזקיה. The extra forty loaves are insurance in case the first forty are lost or become impure.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה makes forty out of eighty holy all at once, against רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה holds the owner wanted only forty holy and brought the rest as a backup, so no simultaneous holiness is involved.
